title: Chapter 0: GP referral to treatment (synthetic)
description: Synthetic slice of one GP practice, a referral office, one outpatient specialist and one scanner. All values are modelling choices, not claims about the Dutch system; see docs/EVIDENCE_AND_ASSUMPTIONS.md.

treeknormWeeks.rationale: Fixed 12-week threshold from SIMULATION_SPEC section 5; not asserted as a verified citation (E-01/E-02 are unverified).

abandonmentExtraWeeks.rationale: Default abandonment delay beyond the 12-week Treeknorm (24 weeks after referral in total), SIM_CONTRACTS section 'Data contracts'.

arrivalsPerWeek.rationale: Mean GP demand arrivals per week (Poisson) for the ~600-resident cohort (A-01); chosen for playable queues.

pUrgent.rationale: Share of arrivals assigned urgent priority at arrival.

pReferral.rationale: Share of GP consults ending in a specialist referral; chosen with outpatient and diagnostics service times to make the baseline scanner load about 0.9 (A-02).

pDiagnostics.rationale: Probability the outpatient consult orders diagnostics; single modality, tuned with the baseline outpatient capacity for scanner load about 0.9 (A-03).

gpReworkMeanMinutes.rationale: Mean GP admin time to complete and re-send an incomplete referral.

followupMeanMinutes.rationale: Mean outpatient follow-up consult after diagnostics.

gpAdminBurden.method: Carried over from legacy Cammelot IST value; source quality not re-checked.

diagnosticsRho.rationale: Chosen for the slice's baseline queueing thesis; not a measured real-world value.

referralCompletenessIntegrated.rationale: Experiment parameter; ramps over one quarter.

startingBudgetEur.rationale: Across three sources; not derived from IZA per-capita share.

areas.label: GP practice
areas.rationale: One GP seat for the cohort; lognormal service time with CV 0.5 (A-09). Admin burden is not modelled separately in this phase.

areas.label: Hospital referral office
areas.rationale: One admin triage server; lognormal service time with CV 0.5 (A-09).

areas.label: Outpatient clinic
areas.rationale: One specialist; 30 consult slots/week at the stated hours, lognormal service time with CV 0.5 (A-09).

areas.label: Diagnostics scanner
areas.rationale: One scanner (equipment 1) staffed by one technician seat (servers 1) with a morning slice allocated to this cohort; default expected rho is about 0.9 (A-02). Capacity is min(servers, equipment), so a new scanner needs a technician and vice versa.

infrastructure.rationale: Referral completeness baseline 70% (A-04) and one-day transfer latency. manualHandoffRate and failureRate are reserved for later phases and not used by the phase-2 engine.

fundingSources.label: Ministerial discretionary
fundingSources.rationale: Flexible source; its political cost is not simulated yet.

fundingSources.label: Earmarked programme grant
fundingSources.rationale: One-off spend on named intervention types only; not modelled on any real programme.

fundingSources.label: Hospital operating budget
fundingSources.rationale: Recurring staff and maintenance; the three sources total the A-08 budget.

interventions.title: One More Specialist
interventions.rationale: Costs are playable round numbers; recruitment delay and success follow A-06.

variants.label: Recruit an outpatient specialist
variants.mechanism: Adds one staffed outpatient consult seat when the hire arrives. Each consult can order a scan.

variants.label: Reassign a GP session to outpatient
variants.mechanism: Moves one staffed seat from the GP practice to the outpatient clinic from the next day. No new money; the GP practice loses that seat.

variants.label: Recruit a scanner technician
variants.mechanism: Adds one technician seat in diagnostics when the hire arrives. Scans still need a free scanner.

interventions.title: New Scanner Wing
interventions.rationale: Two-quarter construction and playable round-number capital and maintenance costs.
interventions.mechanism: Adds one scanner (equipment) after construction. A scanner only scans when a technician seat is free to run it.

interventions.title: Connect the Referral Flow
interventions.rationale: One-quarter implementation then a one-quarter adoption ramp to the A-05 completeness; playable one-off cost.
interventions.mechanism: Raises GP-to-hospital referral completeness from 70% towards 92% as adoption ramps, so fewer referrals bounce back for GP rework. Adds no clinical capacity.
